pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: The sender’s need. Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Message A · simulated source
pages.subject: A quick reply
paragraphs: “Please send a quick reply so I can plan the next stage.” The sender explains that long silence makes scheduling difficult. They want to know whether the request has arrived and when an answer can be expected. The message does not explicitly say whether quick means a receipt acknowledgement or a complete verified response.

Their underlying need is predictability. A useful reformulation should preserve that without turning it into a demand for unverified figures. The learner should check the intended meaning before assigning an unreasonable position to the sender. The fact that a request feels urgent does not establish that every part of it must be completed immediately.

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: The receiver’s concern. Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Message B · simulated source
pages.subject: Time to verify
paragraphs: “Verification of the requested figures requires additional time. We cannot give a reliable final answer today.” The receiver is concerned that a quick reply will be treated as a completed check. They want enough time to verify the figures before anyone acts on them. They have not rejected sending a receipt acknowledgement or a realistic estimate.

The dense wording is not inherently incorrect, but it leaves the person and next action less visible. A clearer oral version might say who is checking and when they will respond. The task is to identify the common ground, separate acknowledgement from completion and test a concrete example with both sides before declaring the disagreement resolved.

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: So, if I understand you correctly, verification can still take until tomorrow?

lines.text: Yes, provided the sender gives a realistic time and updates us if it changes
lines.audioText: Yes, provided the sender gives a realistic time and updates us if it changes.
lines.translation: Sim, desde que a pessoa dê um horário realista e avise se mudar

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: To put it another way, a message can be fast without pretending the answer is complete
lines.audioText: To put it another way, a message can be fast without pretending the answer is complete.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Exactly. A concrete example would be: “Received. I’ll check the figures and reply by four tomorrow.”

lines.text: That also makes the next step easier to track than “verification of availability is ongoing”

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: Quick acknowledgement, not unchecked certainty. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. I think my request for a quick reply has been misunderstood. I wasn’t asking for the checked figures today. I was asking for a prompt acknowledgement and a realistic time for the complete answer. If verification takes until four tomorrow, please say that. What’s difficult is silence, followed by a rushed answer that looks final but hasn’t been checked. Could you explain both positions again so they can see the common ground? One person is protecting accuracy; the other is trying to plan around a response. A useful reformulation should make those needs visible and give an example, rather than repeat the word quick more loudly. Please check that they agree with your summary before treating it as their settled position
